sections.html:
Middletown Township sells like a large shore suburb with one gate every seller passes through: a Residential Certificate of Occupancy that must be issued before title transfers. Start that inspection early, then fit the rest of the sale around it.

The township has about 67,135 residents and 25,211 households. Roughly 85.7 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, the median owner value is $608,300, and median household income is $141,810. Workers spend an average of 34.9 minutes getting to their jobs, which fits a township built around commuter rail, ferries and the Garden State Parkway.

Addresses read "Middletown," but local descriptions use section names such as Belford, Lincroft, Fairview, Leonardo, Navesink, New Monmouth and Port Monmouth. Houses from different eras carry different electrical, plumbing and addition histories, so pull the permit record before the inspector arrives.

sections.h2: Certificate of Occupancy application and fees
sections.html:
Middletown requires a Certificate of Occupancy before transfer of title, and violators may face fines or a summons. The same form covers a sale or a rental, goes to the Housing Department at 1 Kings Highway, and asks for the block, lot, number of bedrooms and the prospective transfer date. If the house is occupied, an adult must be home for the inspection, and the visit time depends on the inspector's daily workload.

Charges on the Middletown certificate of occupancy application.
ChargeAmountNotes
Certificate of occupancy fee$150Non-refundable, one fee for each sale or rental unit
Filing fee$15Paid by a separate check from the $150
Reinspection fee$75Applies at the third inspection
Smoke and carbon monoxide certificateSet by Fire PreventionIssued by the Fire Prevention Office as part of the certificate

The township also lists a 60-Day Conditional Residential Certificate of Occupancy form. Ask Building & Inspection at (732) 615-2104 whether it fits a sale where the buyer plans to make repairs after closing.

The township's checklist follows the International Property Maintenance Code and is not all inclusive, so other items can be noted on the day. Open permits need a final inspection, and recent construction needs approvals before a certificate can issue.

  • Address numbers at least 4 inches high, readable from the street.
  • A water heater relief valve discharge pipe ending no more than 6 inches above the floor, in copper, galvanized, black or CPVC pipe. PVC is not permitted.
  • Ground fault outlets in the garage, outdoors, on kitchen counters, in unfinished basements and in bathrooms, plus no extension cords in place of wiring.
  • Handrails where stairs have more than four risers, and guards on any open side more than 30 inches above grade.
  • A metal flex hose on the dryer, working burners on the range and no leaks or missing shingles on the roof.
  • A debris-free yard, no peeling exterior paint, a septic system that is not visibly failing, and a self-latching 48 inch barrier around any pool deeper than 24 inches.

The Fire Prevention Office at 732-615-2270 inspects smoke detector and carbon monoxide compliance, and the Building & Inspection Department issues the certificate once every requirement is met.

Buyers rank Middletown by how it gets them to New York, and the township offers more than one route.

  • Rail: NJ Transit's Middletown station sits on the North Jersey Coast Line between New York Penn Station and Bay Head.
  • Ferry: NY Waterway runs from a slip in Belford, a trip of roughly 50 minutes to West Midtown, and SeaStreak sails from neighboring Highlands.
  • Roads: Garden State Parkway exits 109 and 114, Routes 35 and 36, and County Routes 516 and 520.
  • Bus: NJ Transit local routes 817, 833 and 834.

A buyer's inspector will look hard at roofs, gutters and grading in a shore town. Elevation certificates are needed for new construction in mapped flood zones, so ask the township floodplain manager whether your lot sits in one.

If you think the assessment is too high, act early because the window is short. Monmouth County follows an alternative assessment calendar, so an assessment appeal must be received, not just postmarked, by the County Tax Board on or before January 15. A separate petition goes in for each parcel, the owner needs three to five comparable sales, and hearings run from January through April. Taxes themselves cannot be appealed, only the assessment, and a change-of-assessment postcard gives 45 days to file.

The state charges the seller a Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded, and the amount rises with the price. Deeds above $1,000,000 add a graduated percent fee of 1 percent to 3.5 percent of the full price. Deeds between spouses, parent and child, or from an estate to an heir are among the listed exemptions.

sections.h2: Where a Middletown deed is recorded
sections.html:
Deeds for Middletown are recorded with the Monmouth County Clerk in Freehold. The fee is $40 for the first page of a deed, $10 for each additional page and $10 for a marginal notation, and transfer tax must be paid when the deed is recorded. Mortgage discharges are $30 for the first page and $10 for each added page, so ask your closing agent which pieces are being filed.

Deeds over $1,000,000 received after July 10, 2025 may be subject to a revised transfer fee under P.L. 2025, c. 69. Anyone selling a higher priced home should confirm the amount with the Division of Taxation before closing.

sections.h2: Sequence for a quick Middletown sale
sections.html:
Call Building & Inspection first and request the permit history for the house. Close any open permits, because a final inspection is required before the certificate can issue. Next, submit the application with the $150 fee and the separate $15 filing check, and ask Fire Prevention to schedule the smoke and carbon monoxide inspection.

Walk the house with the checklist above before the inspector does. Fixing a missing dryer hose, an unprotected outlet near a sink or a peeling porch rail ahead of time can save you the $75 reinspection charge. Keep an adult available on the inspection day.

On closing day the title company or attorney collects the transfer fee and sends the deed to the county clerk. Bring the certificate of occupancy, the smoke and carbon monoxide approval and any permit closeouts so the buyer's side has a complete file, including anything the township asks to see again, and nothing waits on a missing signature.

A cash buyer who takes the house as is can still need the certificate, and the 60-Day Conditional form may let repairs continue after closing. Ask the township before you sign a contract that promises a closing date.

faqs.q: How much does a Middletown certificate of occupancy cost?
faqs.a: The township application lists $150 for each house sold, plus a $15 filing fee on a separate check. A reinspection at the third inspection costs $75.

faqs.q: Who issues the smoke and carbon monoxide certificate in Middletown?
faqs.a: The Fire Prevention Office handles it as part of the Residential Certificate of Occupancy. Building & Inspection issues the final certificate once everything is met.

faqs.q: What is the Middletown deadline to appeal an assessment?
faqs.a: January 15. Monmouth County uses an alternative calendar, and the petition must be received by the County Tax Board, not just mailed, with separate paper copies to the assessor and municipal clerk.

faqs.q: Can a Middletown house with open permits still sell?
faqs.a: It can go under contract, but open permits need a final inspection before a certificate of occupancy can issue. Ask Building & Inspection for the permit history before you list.

faqs.q: Which office records a Middletown deed?
faqs.a: The Monmouth County Clerk records it. The fee is $40 for the first page and $10 for each additional page, and the seller's Realty Transfer Fee is paid at recording.
